title: Orchestrator reentrancy safeguards and result propagation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: our tool execution orchestrator currently allows multi-tool chains and result injection but lacks robust reentrancy and loop-guard protections. This leads to two classes of issues: 1) accidental recursive tool invocations (infinite loops or runaway token costs) when tools call back into the orchestrator via function calls or webhooks, and 2) inconsistent provenance for injected results when streaming partial tool outputs into the LLM context. Goal: provide a pragmatic set of guards and propagation conventions that prevent recursion loops, make result provenance explicit (for streaming and non-streaming flows), and maintain compatibility with older tool interfaces used by customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Orchestrator rejects tool-invoked requests that exceed recursion depth N (configurable per-customer) with a clear error code and metric.
2) Every injected tool result (streamed or final) includes a provenance header (tool_id, call_id, parent_call_stack) available in the console and logs.
3) Backwards-compatible mode for legacy tools: if tool advertises legacy_interface=true, orchestrator applies soft-guards (warnings + throttling) instead of hard-rejects.
4) Unit and integration tests covering nested chains up to depth N+1, result streaming with partial-chunk injection, and idempotency tokens for retry semantics.
design_notes:
High-level approach:
- Call stack metadata: attach a lightweight call-trace token to every request (uuid + short path). The token is propagated into tool calls and returned with results. Use a concise base64 path to avoid payload bloat.
- Recursion detection: compute a hash fingerprint of the call-trace path. If a new invocation would re-use any ancestor tool_id + fingerprint pair, reject to avoid loops.
- Depth limit: default depth=6 for hosted API, configurable up to 20 for Dedicated/Private. Policy stored in customer config and enforced by router.
- Idempotency & retry: require optional idempotency_key for tool invocation; if present, subsequent retries will fetch cached results from the tool-result-store rather than re-executing the tool.
- Streaming injection model: stream chunks with a metadata prefix frame that includes provenance headers; the runtime merges these frames into the assistant stream with explicit markers so downstream parsers can correlate tokens to tool chunks.
- Backcompat layer: compatibility adapter that translates older tool response schemas (text-only, no provenance) into new enriched frames by emitting synthetic provenance and marking `legacy: true`.
- Observability: new metrics (recursion_rejects, provenance_missing_count, legacy_tool_warnings) and tracing spans for call propagation.
tradeoffs_and_rationale:
- Hard rejects are safest but will break some legacy customer automation; hence we provide a soft-guard mode.
- Adding provenance to every stream chunk increases per-request metadata, slightly affecting throughput; mitigated by compact encoding and sampling for high-throughput customers.
- Hash-based loop detection is probabilistic but fast; we accept a tiny false positive rate to avoid expensive graph traversals at runtime.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints):
- Implement call-trace token propagation in orchestrator and SDK middleware (ENG)
- Implement recursion fingerprint check + configurable depth enforcement (ENG)
- Add idempotency_key plumbing and cache hooks (infra)
Phase 2 (1 sprint):
- Streaming provenance frames and console parsing (runtime + console)
- Compatibility adapter for legacy tools (tooling)
Phase 3 (1 sprint):
- Telemetry, metrics, alerting, and rollout to dedicated tiers with gradual ramp.

Key repos/PRs:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TOOL/Execution+Loop+Reentrancy+Design
- GH prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1423
- SDK middleware changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/608
- Console parsing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/321
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprinting and depth logic.
- Integration tests simulating multi-tool chains, including a synthetic tool that calls back into the orchestrator to exercise reentrancy.
- Load test with streaming enabled to measure metadata overhead (target <4% p99 latency regression).
- Chaos test: introduce noise in call-trace propagation to ensure graceful degradation.
- QA checklist: verify provenance shows up in Console request detail, confirm legacy_adapter toggles, confirm error codes and metrics.
rollout_notes:
- Default: enable hard-guards for new accounts; existing accounts start with soft-guards and 60-day migration window.
- Feature flag gate in runtime to toggle hard vs soft behavior per-account.
- Monitor metrics channel #runtime-ops for spikes in recursion_rejects during rollout.
- Provide an opt-out header for emergency compatibility in Private deployments.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: false positives in fingerprinting can break valid nested orchestration. Mitigation: start with a conservative default threshold and allow customer opt-ins; expose a debugging flag that emits full call-path to logs for manual inspection.
Risk: increased token latency for streaming due to extra frames. Mitigation: compact frame encoding and per-customer sampling for detailed provenance.
follow_ups:
- Post-launch: explore declarative tool contracts that can express allowed reentrancy (e.g., stateless vs stateful tools).
- Evaluate using Merkle-style incremental fingerprints to reduce false positives.
- Add SDK helpers to visualize call graphs for debugging in Console.
